Given that $\overset{―}{CE}$ is a segment, what is the measure of $∠DOC?$

q-237390.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14190698/assets/4f0f4b52fc5b84d2d63281da0bc8d92f7433a248550e81c27b0a92a6e5d58a34.png)

Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to ${180}^{∘},$ a straight angle.

Since $\overset{―}{CE}$ is a segment, we have that $∠DOE$ and $∠DOC$ are supplementary. 

$$
m∠DOE+m∠DOC={180}^{∘}
$$

Therefore, the measure of $∠DOC$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠DOC & ={180}^{∘}-m∠DOE \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{67}^{∘} \\  & ={113}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

q-237426.problem: The measure of the angle that forms a linear pair with the angle of ${27}^{∘}$ is{{field-1}}${}^{∘}.$
q-237426.worked_solution:
If two angles form a linear pair, the sum of their measures is equal to ${180}^{∘}.$ 

So, the measure of an angle forming a linear pair with an angle of ${27}^{∘}$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}-{27}^{∘} & ={153}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-116947.name: Question 8
q-116947.problem: Find the measure of an angle that's supplementary to an angle of $(2x+65)^{∘}.$
q-116947.worked_solution:
Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to ${180}^{∘}.$ 

So, the measure of an angle that's supplementary to an angle of $(2x+65)^{∘}$ must be

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}-(2x+65)^{∘} & =(180-2x-65)^{∘} \\  & =(180-65-2x)^{∘} \\  & =(115-2x)^{∘}.\end{aligned}

q-116947.html:
Question 8
?

Find the measure of an angle that's supplementary to an angle of (2x+65)∘.

a
(155−2x)∘
b
(115−2x)∘
c
(245−2x)∘
d
(95−2x)∘
e
(25−2x)∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to 180∘.

So, the measure of an angle that's supplementary to an angle of (2x+65)∘ must be

180∘−(2x+65)∘=(180−2x−65)∘=(180−65−2x)∘=(115−2x)∘.

Solve for $x$ given the figure above.
q-5920.worked_solution:
Since the two angles are supplementary, the sum of their measures is equal to ${180}^{∘}.$ Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}{40}^{∘}+(5x+{20}^{∘}) & ={180}^{∘} \\ 5x+{60}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 5x & ={120}^{∘} \\ x & ={24}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
